traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and REQ-AUTOFIX-* requirements in docs/stories/008.0-DEV-AUTO-FIX.story.md are fully implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality: ESLint `--fix` resolves common annotation violations via `traceability/require-story-annotation` (inserting missing @story for functions/methods/TS variants) and `traceability/valid-annotation-format` (safe @story suffix normalization). Behavior is explicitly exercised and passing in tests/rules/auto-fix-behavior-008.test.ts. - Quality & Safety: Tests show fixes are conservative: already-correct code is unchanged; only clearly safe cases are auto-fixed; complex/ambiguous formats remain diagnostics-only. Helper tests confirm insertion locations and minimal text edits, ensuring no runtime behavior changes. - Integration: The rules are part of the plugin’s normal rule set and presets; integration tests (CLI and config) all pass, confirming auto-fix behavior works in the ESLint toolchain and via the plugin’s recommended configuration. - User Experience: Tests cover multiple function/method/TS patterns and simple suffix patterns, verifying consistent, predictable before/after behavior. When `autoFix` is disabled, diagnostics remain but no edits occur, matching the story’s selective control requirement. - Error Handling: Where fixes cannot be applied safely, the rules only report errors; the test suite contains numerous invalid cases for both rules, with no evidence of unsafe fixes being attempted, aligning with REQ-AUTOFIX-SAFE and the Error Handling acceptance criterion. - Documentation: user-docs/api-reference.md documents the auto-fix behavior, configuration options (templates and autoFix toggles), safety constraints, and example usage for both rules, satisfying the Documentation acceptance criterion.
Tests for this story and its supporting rules all pass in the current Jest run, and the story file itself matches the assessed specification. Therefore this story is fully implemented and passes.
